objective: Dry run of the M1 tier A gates without the game (FB-33-03): show that the build check, the read-only snapshots, the ETW network monitoring and the outcome rules give the predeclared outcome for a clean session and for each injected fault, before the owner decides on tier A.
hypothesis: Run elevated, all 11 cases give their expected outcome: baseline PASS; start build changed NOT RUN; DLL changed during the session, unexpected write, save removed, position not following the movement, unexpected online contact (one UDP datagram to TEST-NET-1 192.0.2.1) and unclean exit FAIL; ambiguous provenance, no data and lost monitoring (no end canary) INCONCLUSIVE. Run without elevation, the trace cannot start, so every case that depends on network coverage is INCONCLUSIVE (baseline, position not following, online contact, lost monitoring, ambiguous provenance, no data), NOT RUN stays NOT RUN, and the other FAIL cases stay FAIL.
environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, Python 3.15, logman and tracerpt from Windows; fixtures in a temporary directory; the stand-in is tools/m1/standin.py, not the game
game_exe_sha256: N/A (the dry run never touches the game, its files or its saves)
procedure: python -I tools/m1/dryrun.py, once without elevation (Claude Code) and once from an elevated PowerShell (the owner; the auto-mode classifier refused an elevation launched by Claude Code). Each case builds a fixture install, fixture config, log and save folders, takes a build check and a snapshot, starts the trace (netwatch start), runs the stand-in, injects its fault, stops the trace (netwatch stop), analyzes it for the stand-in PID, re-checks and re-snapshots, reads the positions from the fixture log and classifies with session.classify. Expected outcomes are fixed in tools/m1/dryrun.py CASES before the runs. The output is evidence/logs/m1-dryrun-<time>-<elevated|not-elevated>/result.json; raw traces are deleted. Before the runs, four read-only Codex passes over the tools found 20 defects (false passes, PID reuse, truncated or unreadable trace files, raw-trace cleanup, invalid tolerances, coordinates and action intervals, order-dependent endpoints, port recording); all were fixed with self-checks in tools/m1/test_m1.py (14 tests).
observed_result: Without elevation (Claude Code, clean commit 16a2b7e): all 11 cases matched their expected outcome (evidence/logs/m1-dryrun-2026-10-27-023424-not-elevated). The trace could not start, so baseline, ambiguous provenance, no data, position not following, online contact and lost monitoring were INCONCLUSIVE; start build changed NOT RUN; DLL changed, unexpected write, save removed and unclean exit FAIL. The elevated run, which must give the baseline PASS and the online-contact FAIL, has not run yet: it waits for the owner, after EXP-044 on the KI-35 branch, because system-wide network tracing could disturb that timing experiment. Re-run without elevation on 60ae022, after review #34 added the per-case required reason (REASONS) and the raw-trace rules: 11/11 match again (evidence/logs/m1-dryrun-2026-10-27-031611-not-elevated; dirty only by the EXP-046 result written seconds before). The elevated run will use 60ae022 or later. Elevated (the owner, clean commit b500439, after EXP-044 and its test battery had finished): all 11 cases matched their expected outcome, each for its predeclared reason (evidence/logs/m1-dryrun-2026-10-27-100820-elevated). The baseline was PASS with the network verdict clean (both canaries seen, 0 events lost); the online-contact case was FAIL on 'unexpected online contact' (one UDP datagram, event 42, IPv4, non-loopback peer); lost monitoring was INCONCLUSIVE on 'end canary not fully seen'; the other cases matched as in the non-elevated runs, now with a clean network verdict. No raw trace was left in any case.
errors: None in the runs. A trace launched elevated by Claude Code was refused by the auto-mode classifier, so the owner ran the elevated half.
follow_up: ChatGPT review of the method and the dry run; then the owner's decision on M1 tier A. The real-game game_written folders, tolerances and actions are fixed in the M1 predeclaration, not here.
